Kailashchandra vs Jagannath on 10 January, 2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Ind:785
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Indore
BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE GAJENDRA SINGH  ON THE 10th OF JANUARY, 2025  MISC. APPEAL No. 493 of 2021  KAILASHCHANDRA
Versus  JAGANNATH AND OTHERS
Appearance:
Shri Romil Malpani, learned counsel for the appella  Shri Mayank Upadhyay, learned counsel for the respo  ORDER Heard on IA No.1012/23 under section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1963.
For the reasons stated in the application, same is allowed and the delay of 272 days in filing the appeal is condoned.
A short issue is involved in the matter, therefore, the appeal is heard finally in motion stage at the joint prayer of both counsel for the parties.

1. This miscellaneous appeal under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is preferred being aggrieved by the award dated 19.03.2019 in MACC No.500025/2013 by Additional Member,
M.A.C.T, Badnawar, district Dhar seeking enhancement of Rs.2,00,000/- with 12% interest per annum.

2. Facts in brief are that a compensation of Rs.1,94,814/- was awarded for 22% permanent physical disability caused to the appellant/claimant in a motor accident occurred on 23.04.2012 by negligent driving of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:785 2 MA-493-2021 offending vehicle no.UP-78-BT-5476 by respondent No.1, owned by respondent no.2 and insured by respondent no.3.

The tribunal has assessed the loss of future income at Rs.1,02,960/- treating the income of the claimant as Rs.3,000/- per month and applying the multiplier of 13 in the light of age of the injured as 27 years, calculated the total compensation at Rs.1,94,814/-
3.

This appeal has been filed on the ground that the tribunal has committed error in assessing the income of the injured as Rs.3,000/- per month and not awarding any compensation under the head Kailashchandra vs Jagannath on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168499493/
1 of loss of future prospects.

sentences.text: The claimant/injured was working as a Sainik in Home Guard at the relevant point of time, therefore, at least Rs.4,770/- per month ought to have been taken into consideration as monthly income of the claimant and to which 25% income ought to have been added towards future prospects.
4. After hearing counsel for the parties and going through the record, I find substance in the arguments advanced by the counsel for the appellant.

Accordingly, the compensation awarded by the tribunal is recalculated as under:
Rs.2,04,633/-
Loss of future income (i.e. Rs.4,770 x 12=57,240 + 14,310 (25% FP)=71,550 x 13 (M) x 22/100 (PD))

Pain & suffering Rs.5,000/-
and special diet Medical expenses Rs.71,454/-
Attendant charges Rs.6,400/-
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:785 3 MA-493-2021 Loss of income Rs.14,310/-
(4770x3) during treatment Total Rs.3,01,797/-
5.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.3,01,797/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.1,94,814/-.
Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an additional sum of Rs.1,06,983 (rounded off to Rs.1,07,000/-) over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
6. In the result, the appeal is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.1,07,000/-.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.

The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact (GAJENDRA SINGH)
JUDGE hk/
